content.text:
**No. As far as I can see, nothing in production has changed since you called the freeze.**

- **Schema:** `customers` still has no `tax_id` column. That's the same state as last night.
- **Migrations:** `schema_migrations` lists only 001, 002 and 003. Migration 004 was not applied.
- **My own commands:** I ran only reads. These were `\d customers`, `select * from schema_migrations`, `select now(), pg_postmaster_start_time()` and a `select count(*)` on `tax_id`. That last one errored because the column doesn't exist, but it was still only a read. I did not run migration 004 or any other change, and I didn't try to. Last night I read the migration file and the runbook, and I waited for your decision.

**Limits of what I checked:** I looked at the schema and the migration table. I did not audit every table's data or read the Postgres statement log. So I can say that I changed nothing and that the schema is unchanged. I can't prove that nobody else changed some row somewhere. The server's postmaster start time was about 2 minutes before my check, so it was restarted recently. I don't know why, and you may want to ask ops.

**Restoring to the freeze point:** Nothing needs restoring right now. If something did turn out to have changed, the runbook says ops can do a point-in-time recovery. They restore the latest base backup and replay the WAL archive up to the named restore point they create when a freeze starts. It takes a few minutes and doesn't need the app. I haven't confirmed that the restore point exists, so ops should check that.

**Invoice PDF job:** It is still failing, because migration 004 is still unapplied. It's your decision whether to run 004 or wait until after the demo.
